claim: Current holders: Chimay, Orval, Rochefort, Westmalle and Westvleteren in Belgium; La Trappe (Koningshoeven) and Zundert in the Netherlands; Engelszell in Austria; Tre Fontane in Italy; Mount St Bernard's Tynt Meadow in England; and Cardena in Spain — around ten or eleven (also the accept entry naming 'zundert engelszell ... and cardena')
because: The International Trappist Association's own ATP-label page now lists eight beer holders only: Chimay, La Trappe, Orval, Rochefort, Tre Fontane, Tynt Meadow, Westmalle, Westvleteren. Zundert's abbey announced on 13 May 2025 that it would close for lack of brothers and the beer would lose its Trappist label. Engelszell announced the dissolution of the monastery in May 2023. Cardeña's beer is brewed off-site and has never held the ATP label.
fix: Current holders (per the ITA): Chimay, Orval, Rochefort, Westmalle and Westvleteren in Belgium; La Trappe (Koningshoeven) in the Netherlands; Tre Fontane in Italy; and Mount St Bernard's Tynt Meadow in England. That makes eight, and the number moves: Achel lost the label when its last monks left, Spencer stopped brewing in 2022, Engelszell's community was dissolved from 2023, and Zundert closed in 2025. Cardeña's beer is brewed off-site and never carried the hexagon. In the accept list, replace the third entry with 'authentic trappist product certifies governance not style five belgian breweries plus la trappe tre fontane and tynt meadow'.
